newsitem.title: USA: Dove Entertainment sees Q1 loss.
newsitem.headline: Dove Entertainment sees Q1 loss.

text.p: Dove Entertainment Inc said Tuesday it expects to post a loss in the first quarter.

It said it had experienced "severe liquidity pressures" from its poorly-performing audio and book operations. It said its liquidity was also hurt by cash requirements to fund new film and television productions.
The lack of liquidity meant the publication of a number of spring titles was delayed until an equity infusion was finalized, it said.
Dove said it expects the rest of 1997 "to be a period of stabilization."
The company, reporting a loss of the full year 1996, cited, in part, heavy returns and flat sales at its audio and book operations, together with higher overhead costs associated with an expansion.

Heavy returns associated with publications associated with the O.J. Simpson and Menendez brothers trials resulted in an inventory and production cost write-off of $1.9 million and narrower gross margins, the company said.

"The company believes that its results were affected by the market as a whole, which appears to have experienced unusually heavy returns during the year, resulting in a saturated remainder market," Dove said.

It said print publishing successes included Larry Flynt's "An Unseemly Man" and Richard Hack's "When Money is King." It said audio successes included the Grammy award-winning "Rush Limbaugh is a Big Fat Idiot and Other Observations" by Al Franken, and "Exclusive" by Sandra Brown.
